renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: binned_contact_map
  title: Chromosome contact map
  description: |-
    Each cell is a pair of genomic bins on one chromosome, coloured by the balanced contact frequency between them, with position on both axes. It answers how the chromosome folds: which regions touch each other more than their distance predicts.
    How to read: the diagonal is always brightest because neighbouring bins contact most, and contact falls away with distance. Squares along the diagonal are self-interacting domains, and bright spots off the diagonal are loops or long-range contacts. The map re-bins to a finer resolution as you zoom in.
    Lines and annotations: the colour scale is logarithmic, since contact frequency spans several orders of magnitude. The values are balanced with the ICE method, which removes per-bin coverage biases, so a bin is comparable with another.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22941365/
  kind: contact_map
  config:
    log_scale: true
  roles:
    chrom1: chrom1
    start1: start1
    chrom2: chrom2
    start2: start2
    count: count
    resolution: resolution
    sample: sample

- component: card
  title: Chromosomes and contacts
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of chromosomes in view, with the number of bin pairs measured next to it. It answers how much of the genome the matrix covers.
    How to read: a coarser resolution has fewer bin pairs. The number of pairs grows as the bins get finer, so compare resolutions with this in mind.
  column: chrom1
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: contacts measured

- component: card
  title: Balanced contact frequency
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median balanced contact frequency over the bin pairs in view, with the lowest and highest values next to it. It answers the typical strength of a contact and how far it spans.
    How to read: contact values span several orders of magnitude, from strong neighbour contacts to faint long-range ones, so the median sits far below the maximum. Compare samples at the same resolution only.
    Note: balanced values are relative contact frequencies and not read counts, so their scale depends on the resolution.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22941365/
  column: count
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: balanced contact, lowest to highest

- component: table
  title: Contact table
  description: |-
    Each row is a pair of bins with its sample, resolution, coordinates and balanced contact frequency. It answers the exact value of any contact on the map.
    How to read: filter to one sample, resolution and chromosome, and sort by contact to list the strongest pairs.
